park_text: Up to iron, each fusion makes nucleons more tightly bound and releases energy; past iron, the products are less tightly bound per nucleon, so fusion would cost energy.

park_text: Uranium sits on the slope below the peak on the heavy side and light nuclei sit far down on the light side; splitting one or joining the others moves the nucleons up toward the peak, and the gain in binding is released.
